summary: Preinstall dropper downloads Bun runtime and executes obfuscated payload
details: The package's package.json preinstall hook runs setup.mjs, an obfuscated script that downloads the Bun runtime from https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v<version>/<platform>.zip, extracts and chmods it executable, and then invokes it via execFileSync to run the sibling file math_init.js. math_init.js is a 727KB heavily obfuscated JavaScript blob using a shuffled string-array loader (WV8StW/n7gIxM, the obfuscator.io pattern). An ESLint React config package has no legitimate reason to ship a preinstall hook that fetches an alternate JavaScript runtime and uses it to execute a large opaque bundled payload on the installer's machine. Both setup.mjs and math_init.js use mangled _0xXXXX identifiers and string-array dispatch, hiding the payload's actual behavior. This is the alternate-runtime dropper pattern: the Bun download itself is from an official source, but the fetched runtime is used to execute the package's own shipped opaque payload at install time, bypassing normal Node review and giving attacker-controlled code execution on every install.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
